questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Other

questions.question: Please explain: *
questions.answer: I have always dreamed of traveling and living in Australia

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: My dream about travelling Australia

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was actually a bit difficult and quite messy. It was hard to figure out where to find information and then when you did figure it out, it was still a bit difficult to understand what was actually meant.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: we contacted the student advisor we had been put in touch with via the application

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: It was actually kind of bad. Often you were simply referred to a previous email, as if you hadn't read what you received. so it was a bit difficult to get direct and concrete answers from them.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
I feel like we were really lucky. we wrote to a few people before we found an apartment. but there was a huge housing crisis so there were a lot of people who had a really hard time finding housing.
We found our apartment on
flatmates.com
, which works really well.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: There are good transportation options by tram. I bought a bike, which I was really happy about - although they really aren't used to cyclists, so you have to pay serious attention.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: i reckon it was very easy and straightforward

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: first you signed up for subjects, and once you had been assigned them, you had to sign up for specific classes, so you largely shaped your schedule yourself

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: They call it "stop 1", where you could go and there would be someone to guide you through the whole process.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got it the way I wanted it. In some cases, I couldn't get the specific class I wanted in the first place, but I was on a waiting list, which meant that in the end I got everything I had hoped for.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: selvom man ikke får det som man ønskede til at starte med, så skal man seriøst bare melde så på de der lister, og så virker det som om, at det løser sig for de fleste.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: they start earlier at uni so first year subjects were quite introductory at a very general level to uni

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: In general, it was much the same. with lectures and then smaller classes for discussions.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
History and philosophy of science
Organisational behavior
Seualising society

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: sexualizing society! It was seriously exciting and provided the basis for some interesting discussions both in class, but also discussions I took home with me.

questions.answer: all kinds of water sports, a lot of opportunities for ball games and a lot of other outdoor activities

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend the mountaineering club

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Tasmania!!!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: i reckon it was pretty easy

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: it was just really hard to get in touch with local students and I never really succeeded

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: can't think of anything off the top of my head

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: they are very sharing but in a very superficially way

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: You're coming to an amazing city with so many opportunities, so it's all about getting out and experiencing it, but at the same time the art of limitation is really important, so you can accept that you can do what you can do without stressing about what you can't do.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: there are some really good reading rooms and the lecturers are quite easy to get in touch with, so you really shouldn't hesitate

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: all the possibilities of the city and just an hour outside

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: it took a while to land mentally, which made it a little difficult to be present at the beginning of the stay. but once you got over it, it was so good.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
